summary: Observability agent service-account impersonation denied due to cross-cloud IAM conditional mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of observability agents (metrics/traces collectors) running in the Dedicated fleet are failing to push telemetry because they cannot impersonate the GCP service account when routed via the AWS STS->GCP broker. This started after a recent org-policy/IAM cleanup that added attribute-based conditionals on serviceAccount impersonation roles.

Impact:
- Production metrics and traces missing for ~6 Dedicated customers in us-east and eu-west regions for ~36 hours.
- Alerts suppressed for affected tenant routes; engineering oncall escalations generated.
- No customer-facing requests reported yet, but internal SLAs for observability were violated.

Environment:
- prod | us-east, eu-west
- Dedicated fleet (redwood-dedicated-prod), STS identity broker between AWS account A and GCP org.
- Affected component: observability-agent container image: redwood/obs-agent:v2.1.4
steps_to_reproduce: 1) From an affected dedicated node, run: gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-observability@customer-project.iam.gserviceaccount.com
2) Observe IAM denial: 'Request had insufficient authentication scopes' or 'Permission iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied'.

3) Trace path through STS broker: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/redwood-sts-broker -> broker uses workload identity federation to exchange credentials for GCP impersonation.
4) Reproduce intermittently depending on which broker instance and GCP org policy evaluation path is used.
logs:
2026-03-10T02:12:14Z obs-agent[pid=4378]: ERROR: impersonation failed: iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken denied for sa-observability@customer-project.
    (requestor: sts-broker-arn:aws:sts::ACCOUNT:assumed-role/redwood-sts-broker/session)

2026-03-10T02:12:14Z broker[info]: federated token exchange success -> attempting gcloud impersonate -> IAM DENY response: 'Permission denied. Condition "resource.name.startsWith('projects/_/serviceAccounts/')" not satisfied'
2026-03-10T02:45:01Z gce-audit[warning]: orgPolicy: constraint 'iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains' enforced; conditional binding present on roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
comments: Support (Rajesh Patel) 2026-03-10: Triage - observed spike in obs-agent 'impersonation failed' errors. Opening cross-team Slack #infra-iam and paging SRE.

SRE (Marta Alvarez) 2026-03-10: Initial hypothesis - recent org-level conditional binding added to service account token creator role; may be matching on resource.name vs resource.service. Asking Cloud Infra to export binding conditions.

Cloud Infra (Tobias Nguyen) 2026-03-11: Confirmed conditional exists on project-level role binding applied by terraform module 'iam/roles-v2'. Condition expression uses request.auth.aud and resource.name mismatch when using federation via STS broker. Working on repro and mitigation plan.

Support (Emily Chen) 2026-03-12: Working mitigation - temporarily relax conditional on dedicated broker principal in staging, then apply to prod after validation. Will coordinate a short maintenance window and notify customers if needed.
investigation_notes: - Root cause: Org-level IAM conditional added to restrict iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator to calls where resource.name matches 'projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/serviceAccounts/*' exactly. Workload identity broker exchanges credentials via federated principal path that results in a slightly different resource.name evaluation path, causing condition to fail.
- Reproduced locally by using the broker's federated token with alterted audience claim -> condition evaluation fails only for broker-issued tokens.

- Also observed a related org-policy enforcement that denies certain federated principals unless an attribute 'broker_id' is present in the condition. The broker did not add this attribute in its token exchange flow.

- Affected customers: dedicated tenants on redwood-dedicated-prod whose telemetry pipeline uses broker instance group a/b. Not all instances affected because some broker instances include additional claims.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied 2026-03-12 03:40 UTC: Temporarily updated terraform 'iam/roles-v2' module to add an exception for arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT:role/redwood-sts-broker with a condition that matches the broker's token attributes.

Follow-up permanent fix: (1) Update STS broker to include 'broker_id' and stable audience claim during federation exchange; (2) Add unit/integration test to terraform module to validate conditional expressions against broker tokens; (3) Roll out a policy-change runbook for cross-cloud IAM condition updates.
Post-action: Verified metrics ingestion resumed for affected tenants within 15 minutes of mitigation. Created proposaland PRs for infra and broker changes.
